newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia OMV Istrabenz sees slump in 96 net.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia OMV Istrabenz sees slump in 96 net.

text.p: Slovenian petrol firm OMV Istrabenz Koper said on Thursday it expected 1996 net profit to tumble to 300 million tolars ($2 million) from 1.36 billion tolars in 1995.
Iztok Jelacin, the company's spokesman, told Reuters profits had fallen because of low officially-fixed petrol prices which were less than half those in Italy and Austria.
In Slovenia, a litre of unleaded petrol currently sells for 78.4 tolars ($0.5).
The company is 40 percent owned by Austria's largest industrial group -- OMV AG.
Jelacin said sales rose to 21 billion tolars ($141 million) from 18 billion in 1995.

OMV Istrabenz, a joint venture of Slovenia's Istrabenz, Austria's OMV AG and Croatia's Ina, manages 79 petrol stations in Slovenia and nine in Croatia. The company's market share in Slovenia is about 25 percent.
"We expect to open 10 to 15 new stations in Slovenia this year and two new ones in Croatia," Jelacin said.

Jelacin said preliminary results of Istrabenz, which owns 50 percent of OMV Istrabenz and will be listed on the over-the-counter section of the Ljubljana bourse on February 3, would be calculated at the beginning of February.
